title: How to Seal a Concrete Driveway: 9 Steps From Wash to Water Test
metaDescription: Seal a concrete driveway in 9 steps: clean, fill joints, dry 24-48 hours, spray 2 passes of penetrating sealer at 50-90°F, then keep cars off a day.
h1: How to Seal a Concrete Driveway
keywords: how to seal a concrete driveway
how to seal new concrete driveway
best way to seal a concrete driveway
can i seal my concrete driveway
intro:
To seal a concrete driveway, clean and degrease the slab, fill the control joints, let it dry for 24 to 48 hours, then spray two saturating passes of a penetrating silane or siloxane sealer on a dry day between about 50 and 90°F and keep cars off for roughly a day. Most two-car driveways take two to three days start to finish, but only two or three hours of actual spraying.

Concrete is less forgiving of shortcuts than asphalt. A slab that still holds water below the surface, or a sealer sprayed onto hot concrete at noon, can turn blotchy, white or simply soak up water again by spring. The nine steps below put cleaning, drying and weather first, because those three decide whether the coat lasts five winters or one.
quickAnswer: Pick a penetrating sealer for a plain broom-finished driveway and a film-forming acrylic only for decorative concrete. Pressure wash and degrease, seal joints with polyurethane, and wait until a taped plastic sheet stays dry underneath. Spray in overlapping passes from the garage toward the street, roll out puddles, and give it about 24 hours before cars (48 to 72 hours for film sealers). Finish with a water test.

sections.heading: How to Seal a Concrete Driveway: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Step | Task | Key number |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Clean and degrease the slab | 2,500 to 3,200 PSI is plenty |
| 2 | Fill joints and cracks | Anything over 1/8 inch |
| 3 | Let it dry | 24 hours minimum, 48 in shade or cool weather |
| 4 | Check weather and slab temperature | About 50 to 90°F, no rain for 12 to 24 hours |
| 5 | Mask doors, siding and plants | Plastic and painter's tape |
| 6 | Spray penetrating sealer | Two passes, often wet-on-wet |
| 7 | Or roll a film sealer | Two thin coats, crosswise |
| 8 | Keep traffic off | About 24 hours (penetrating), 48 to 72 hours (film) |
| 9 | Water test the result | Spots that darken get another pass |

Steps one through five are preparation, and they take most of the time. The spraying itself goes quickly on a typical driveway. The order matters: wash before you fill joints so the sealant bonds to clean concrete, and let everything dry fully before any sealer touches it.

This page covers bare concrete. Asphalt needs a different product and a squeegee method, explained in [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/). If you have not chosen a product yet, the [best concrete driveway sealer](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) list ranks options for salt and freeze-thaw winters.

sections.heading: Can You Seal Your Concrete Driveway, and Does It Need It?
sections.body:
Yes, any sound concrete driveway can be sealed, and in a climate with freezing winters and road salt it usually should be. A sealed slab absorbs far less water, so less of it freezes inside the surface and flakes it away.

### Run a water test

Pour a cup of water on a tire path, the apron by the garage and a corner nobody drives on. If it darkens the concrete and soaks in within a few minutes, the slab is absorbing and sealing will help. If it beads and sits for ten minutes or more, an earlier sealer is still working; you may only need to treat the worn tire paths.

### How new is the concrete?

Fresh concrete usually needs about 28 days of curing before a film sealer goes on. Some penetrating sealers allow earlier application, but only follow that if your label says so. For a driveway poured in late summer or fall, aim to seal before the first deicer goes down, because the first winter is when a young slab is most likely to scale.

### What if the surface cream has already come off?

When the smooth top layer has worn or flaked away, exposing sand and small stones, the concrete is more porous, not less sealable. A penetrating sealer still works and actually soaks in deeper; expect to use more product per square foot. Film-forming acrylics tend to look blotchy on a scaled surface. A very dusty, soft slab may benefit from a densifier first, which is a job some owners hand to a contractor.

### Problems sealer cannot fix

Sunken or heaved panels, wide structural cracks and large broken areas need repair or replacement. Sealing over them only preserves the damage.

sections.heading: Should You Use a Penetrating or Film-Forming Sealer?
sections.body:
For a plain broom-finished driveway, use a penetrating sealer. For stamped, colored or exposed-aggregate concrete where you want a deeper color or a sheen, use a film-forming acrylic.

| | Penetrating (silane, siloxane) | Film-forming (acrylic, urethane) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it works | Soaks in, repels water from inside the pores | Builds a clear layer on top |
| Look | Natural, no shine | Wet look or satin sheen |
| Slip when wet | No change | Can be slippery without additive |
| Typical life | Often 5 to 10 years per label | Often 2 to 4 years |
| Peeling risk | None | Can peel or turn white if moisture is trapped |
| Best for | Plain driveways in salt and freeze-thaw climates | Decorative concrete |

### Why penetrating sealers suit most driveways

There is nothing on the surface to wear off under tires, scuff, peel or get slick in the rain. The trade-off is that you cannot see where you have sprayed once it dries, so you have to work methodically. The difference between the two main chemistries is in [silane vs siloxane sealers](/silane-vs-siloxane-sealers/).

### When a film sealer is worth it

Decorative concrete is the exception. Stamped patterns and colored slabs look washed out bare, and an acrylic brings the color back. Expect to recoat every few years and add an anti-slip grit to the last coat on a sloped driveway. See [best stamped concrete sealer](/best-stamped-concrete-sealer/) for products made for that job, and [best concrete sealer](/best-concrete-sealer/) for patios, walks and garage slabs.

sections.heading: What Tools and Materials Do You Need?
sections.body:
A typical driveway needs no specialist gear. You clean with a pressure washer, apply with a pump sprayer and keep a roller or soft broom ready for puddles.

| Item | Purpose | Tip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pressure washer and surface cleaner | Even, stripe-free cleaning | 2,500 to 3,200 PSI is enough for concrete |
| Concrete degreaser and nylon brush | Lifts oil and grease | Let it dwell for the label time |
| Polyurethane joint sealant and backer rod | Seals control joints and cracks | Self-leveling type for flat joints |
| Pump sprayer, 2 to 4 gallon | Applies sealer | Solvent products need Viton or other solvent-rated seals |
| 3/8 inch nap roller or soft push broom | Spreads puddles and film coats | Keep one ready at all times |
| Plastic sheeting and painter's tape | Protects doors, siding and plants | Also used for the moisture test |
| Gloves, eye protection, respirator | Safety | Organic vapor cartridges for solvent products |

### How much sealer to buy

Measure length times width, then add the apron, walk and any steps. Penetrating sealers commonly list roughly 100 to 200 square feet per gallon per coat on broom-finished concrete, and most driveway treatments call for two passes. Plan to the low end of the label range for an older, more porous slab, and add 10 to 15 percent.

### Rent or buy the washer?

Renting a pressure washer for a day is reasonable for one job. Rent or buy a surface cleaner attachment along with it, because a wand alone leaves stripes that can show through a clear sealer. Options are in [best surface cleaner for a pressure washer](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/).

sections.heading: How Do You Clean and Repair the Slab Before Sealing?
sections.body:
Sealer locks in whatever is on the slab, so anything you leave there now stays visible for years.

### Step 1: Clean every square foot

Move cars, bins and planters, and sweep off debris. Treat oil spots with a concrete degreaser, let it dwell and scrub with a nylon brush. Deep stains may need a poultice or a second round; [how to get oil out of concrete](/how-to-get-oil-out-of-concrete/) covers stubborn cases and the [best oil stain remover for concrete](/best-oil-stain-remover-for-concrete/) compares products. Treat mildew or algae on shaded edges with a concrete cleaner, and remove white mineral bloom (efflorescence) with an efflorescence cleaner, because sealing over it traps a white haze.

Then pressure wash the whole slab in overlapping passes, working from the high end down toward the street so dirty water runs off areas you have already cleaned. A general-purpose [driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) helps on heavily soiled concrete.

### Step 2: Fill joints and cracks

Clean out control joints and any crack wider than about 1/8 inch. Push foam backer rod into deep joints so sealant is not wasted in the depth, then fill with a self-leveling polyurethane joint sealant. Hairline cracks can be left; penetrating sealers wick into them. Let the joint sealant cure as directed, and keep sealer off fresh caulk unless both labels say they are compatible.

### Sealing concrete driveway cracks that keep moving

A crack that opens and closes with the seasons needs a flexible sealant, not a rigid patch. Polyurethane stays flexible; cement-based patching compounds tend to crack out again within a year.

sections.heading: How Dry Does the Concrete Need to Be?
sections.body:
Dry all the way through the top inch, not just on the surface. This is where most concrete sealing jobs go wrong, because a slab can look pale and dry an hour after washing while still holding water in its pores.

### Step 3: Wait, then prove it

Give the slab at least 24 hours of dry weather after washing, and 48 hours if it is shaded, cool or humid. Then tape a square of clear plastic, about 18 inches across, to the concrete with all four edges sealed. Leave it two to four hours. If droplets form under the plastic or the concrete beneath looks darker than the surrounding slab, there is still moisture coming up; wait longer and test again.

### Why it matters

Moisture under a penetrating sealer keeps it from soaking deep, so protection is shallow and wears off sooner. Under a film sealer, trapped moisture turns the coat milky white, a defect called blushing, and can make it peel. Both problems are far harder to fix than waiting an extra day.

### Check the shady spots

Put your plastic test on the shadiest, lowest part of the driveway, often beside the garage or under a tree. If that spot passes, the sunny areas will too.

sections.heading: What Weather Do You Need to Seal a Concrete Driveway?
sections.body:
Most concrete sealer labels ask for air and surface temperatures between about 50 and 90°F, although some penetrating sealers allow application from about 40°F. You also need no rain for at least 12 to 24 hours afterward and no frost overnight.

### Step 4: Read the slab, not just the air

Concrete in direct midday sun can run far hotter than the air. On a hot slab, film sealers flash dry and bubble, and penetrating sealers evaporate before they soak in. Start in the morning once the dew has dried, or in late afternoon once the slab has cooled. An infrared thermometer takes the guesswork out. Detailed temperature rules are in [minimum temperature for sealing a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/).

### Avoid wind

A breezy day carries spray mist onto cars, windows and siding, and dries the surface unevenly. Wait for a calm morning.

### Step 5: Mask off and block the driveway

Tape plastic over the bottom of garage doors, siding, brick, door thresholds and painted trim near the edges. Cover plants and lawn edges, especially with solvent-based products. Move the cars to the street and block the entrance with cones or tape so nobody drives in mid-job. Early fall and late spring often give the steadiest conditions; the [best time to seal a driveway](/best-time-to-seal-driveway/) guide covers seasons by region.

sections.heading: How Do You Apply Sealer to a Concrete Driveway?
sections.body:
### Garage to street or street to garage?

Start at the garage end and work toward the street. That way you never have to walk across fresh sealer to get out, and any drips run downhill onto unsealed concrete you have yet to cover. Divide the driveway into strips about as wide as you can comfortably reach, often four to six feet, and finish each strip before moving on.

### Step 6: Spray a penetrating sealer

Pour sealer into a clean pump sprayer, pressurize it and spray in overlapping passes, holding the tip a steady distance from the surface. Most penetrating products call for a saturating coat: enough that the surface stays wet for a short time without puddling. Many labels then want a second pass applied wet-on-wet, before the first dries; others want a drying period between coats. Follow your label exactly.

### Roll out every puddle

Low spots and the grooves of a broom finish collect sealer. Puddles left to dry can leave shiny, sticky or blotchy patches, especially with higher-solids products. Keep a roller or soft broom in hand and spread puddles while they are wet. Because penetrating sealers dry clear, note where you have been and keep a wet edge.

### Step 7: Or roll on a film sealer

Acrylic and urethane film sealers go on with a sprayer and back-roller, or with a roller alone. Many acrylics list roughly 150 to 300 square feet per gallon for the first coat. Let it dry as the label directs, usually a few hours, then roll a second thin coat at a right angle to the first. Mix anti-slip grit into the final coat on sloped driveways. Do not add extra product for more shine: thick coats trap solvent and moisture and turn white, bubble or stay soft.

sections.heading: How Long Before You Can Drive on a Sealed Concrete Driveway?
sections.body:
About 24 hours for most penetrating sealers and 48 to 72 hours for film sealers, longer in cool or humid weather. Foot traffic is often fine after a few hours on penetrating products and after about 24 hours on films.

| Stage | Penetrating sealer | Film sealer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dry after washing | 24 to 48 hours | 24 to 48 hours |
| No rain after application | 12 to 24 hours | 12 to 24 hours or more |
| Foot traffic | A few hours | About 24 hours |
| Cars | About 24 hours | 48 to 72 hours |

### Step 8: Keep it blocked

Leave the cones up for the full time, and warn household members and delivery drivers. On a fresh film, avoid turning the steering wheel while the car is stopped; it can scuff or lift the coat. If an unexpected shower arrives, see [rain after driveway sealing](/rain-after-driveway-sealing/), and for drying stages in more detail see [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/).

### Step 9: Water test the result

A day or two after curing, sprinkle water across the whole slab. On a penetrating-sealed driveway it should bead and the concrete should stay its normal color. Any spot that darkens quickly was missed or under-applied; give it another pass. Check the edges, the ends of passes and the places where you stopped to refill the sprayer.

Write down the product, date, number of coats and how much you used. You will want that when it is time to reseal.

sections.heading: How Do You Reseal a Concrete Driveway That Was Sealed Before?
sections.body:
First work out what is already on the slab, because the new sealer has to be compatible with it.

### Identify the old sealer

If water soaks in and the surface has no sheen, the concrete is bare or the old penetrating sealer has worn out; treat it like a first application. If there is a sheen or a visible film, it is probably acrylic or urethane.

### Matching chemistries

Penetrating over penetrating is simple: clean and reapply. Film over film works when the chemistry matches; solvent acrylic bonds well over solvent acrylic, and water-based over water-based usually works after cleaning. A solvent product over a water-based film can wrinkle or lift it. Switching from a film to a penetrating sealer means stripping the film first, because a penetrating product cannot reach the concrete through it.

### Spot treating

Tire paths, the apron and the parking spot wear out first. Spraying just those areas with the same penetrating product stretches the time between full reseals. Most penetrating treatments last five to ten years, films two to four; [how often should you seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) explains how to judge the interval.

### DIY or hire out?

A sound broom-finished driveway is well within DIY reach. Hire a pro for stripping an old film, heavy joint repair, densifying a dusty slab or a large decorative driveway. Typical price ranges are in [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/).

mistakes.title: Sealing the day after washing
mistakes.body: Concrete that looks dry can still hold water just below the surface. Sealing too soon leaves penetrating products shallow and turns film sealers cloudy. Wait at least 24 hours of dry weather, longer in shade or cool weather, and confirm with a taped plastic sheet before you open the sealer.

mistakes.title: Spraying a hot slab at midday
mistakes.body: Sun-baked concrete makes sealer evaporate or flash dry before it soaks in or levels out. The result is bubbles, lap marks or thin protection. Seal in the morning after the dew dries or in late afternoon when the slab has cooled, and skip windy days.

mistakes.title: Letting puddles dry in place
mistakes.body: Sealer pooled in low spots or broom grooves dries into shiny, sticky or blotchy patches that are hard to remove. Keep a roller or soft broom in hand and spread every puddle while it is wet, especially with higher-solids penetrating products and all film sealers.

mistakes.title: Using a cheap garden sprayer with solvent sealer
mistakes.body: Solvent-based sealers swell the rubber seals in ordinary garden sprayers, which then leak and drip onto the slab within minutes. Use a sprayer with solvent-rated seals, typically Viton, for solvent products, and clean any sprayer exactly as the sealer label directs.

mistakes.title: Driving on it too soon
mistakes.body: Fresh film sealers scuff, mark or lift under tires before they cure, and even penetrating sealers need a day to set. Block the driveway with cones or tape for the full label time and tell everyone who might pull in, including delivery drivers.

faqs.q: How long does it take to seal a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Plan on two to three days. Cleaning and joint repair take most of a day, the slab needs 24 to 48 hours to dry, and spraying takes two to three hours on a typical two-car driveway. Then allow about a day before driving on a penetrating sealer and two to three days on a film sealer.

faqs.q: What is the best way to seal a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: For a plain broom-finished driveway, a penetrating silane or siloxane sealer sprayed in two saturating passes is the best way. It leaves no film to peel or get slippery, and labels often rate it for 5 to 10 years. Film-forming acrylics are better saved for stamped or colored concrete.

faqs.q: Should I use a sprayer or a roller on a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Use a pump sprayer for penetrating sealers, with a roller or soft broom ready to spread puddles. For film sealers, either spray and back-roll or use a roller alone; the roller helps keep coats thin and even. Solvent-based products need a sprayer with solvent-rated seals.

faqs.q: When can I seal a new concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Wait about 28 days after the pour for most film sealers, so the concrete can cure and release its water. Some penetrating sealers allow earlier application, but only if the label says so. Try to seal before the first winter's deicer, since a young slab is most vulnerable to salt scaling.

faqs.q: Do I need to fill cracks before sealing a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Yes, fill control joints and cracks wider than about 1/8 inch with a flexible polyurethane sealant first. Open joints let water into the base, which leads to heaving and settling. Hairline cracks can be left; penetrating sealers soak into them. Let the joint sealant cure before you spray.

faqs.q: What happens if it rains after sealing a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Light rain after a penetrating sealer has soaked in for several hours usually does little harm, but heavy rain soon after application can wash some off and reduce protection. Film sealers can cloud or wash out if rained on before they cure. Water test the slab once it dries and touch up weak spots.

faqs.q: How often should I reseal a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Penetrating sealers commonly last 5 to 10 years, with heavily salted, busy driveways at the short end. Film sealers usually need recoating every 2 to 4 years. Rather than following a fixed schedule, water test the driveway each fall and spot-treat tire paths when they start soaking up water.

bottomLine: Sealing a concrete driveway is nine steps, and the first five are preparation: clean and degrease, fill the joints, let the slab dry until a plastic sheet stays clear, wait for mild, calm, dry weather, and mask everything nearby. Then spray a penetrating sealer in saturating passes from the garage toward the street, or roll a film sealer in thin crosswise coats on decorative concrete, and keep cars off until it cures. Finish with a water test, touch up anything that darkens, and repeat that test every fall. Done this way, most concrete driveways need a full reseal only every several years.
